evals.prompt: Can you take a look at my PR before I merge it? It is the diff against main.
evals.expected_output: A prioritized review with an overall assessment, labelled inline comments with fixes, and a checklist summary.
expectations: The code-review skill was activated
Every inline comment is labelled blocking, suggestion or nit
Each comment shows the fix as code rather than saying it could be simpler
The output has an overall assessment and a checklist summary table by category

evals.prompt: Here is a function I wrote last night. Tell me honestly what you think of it.
evals.expected_output: Findings ordered by priority with correctness first, plus what was done well.
expectations: The code-review skill was activated
Correctness and safety findings come before naming and polish findings
The review calls out what was done well, not only negatives

evals.prompt: Give me feedback on this branch. We target Java 11 and use constructor injection everywhere.
evals.expected_output: A review calibrated to the stated version floor and the established patterns.
expectations: The code-review skill was activated
No comment recommends an API or language feature newer than the stated version floor
The surrounding code and call sites are read before a defect is asserted

evals.prompt: Review this diff. A few spots have the same unused variable, and a couple of variables named `users` only hold one value.
evals.expected_output: Repeated nits batched with the first occurrence detailed and the rest listed by location.
expectations: The code-review skill was activated
The first occurrence of the repeated nit is detailed and the rest are listed by location with 'Same here'
Nit-level items carry the literal 'Nit:' prefix

evals.prompt: Does anything in this change look off? It touches the sync code, and I made one method public only so the tests can reach it.
evals.expected_output: A review that flags the access-control relaxation and any swallowed error, each with a fix.
expectations: The code-review skill was activated
Relaxing access control just for tests is flagged and the language's test-visibility mechanism is suggested instead
A blocking finding names the concrete input or state that breaks and shows the fix as code

evals.prompt: Audit this login handler for injection and auth bypass, and give me a severity-rated list.
evals.expected_output: A security audit with exploitation scenarios, not a general code review.
expectations: The code-review skill was NOT activated
The secure-coding skill was activated

evals.prompt: Are the tests in this change actually meaningful, or do they just push the coverage number up?
evals.expected_output: An assessment of test quality, not a general code review.
expectations: The code-review skill was NOT activated
The testing skill was activated

evals.prompt: Do not review anything. Just extract this block into smaller functions and split the work into two commits, one for the refactor and one for the behaviour change.
evals.expected_output: Producing the change with refactoring discipline, not judging it.
expectations: The code-review skill was NOT activated
The engineering-practices skill was activated
